questions.question: What happens when an external table in Unity Catalog is dropped?
choices: The metadata and every data file are deleted immediately
The data files are moved into the metastore's managed storage location
The table is turned into a volume that holds the same files
The metadata is removed, but the data files stay in storage
questions.explanation: With external tables, Unity Catalog governs the metadata, but you manage the data's lifecycle. After DROP TABLE the files remain at the LOCATION and must be removed separately if they are no longer needed.

questions.question: An engineer needs a Unity Catalog table over existing data at s3://acme-data/erp/orders/. What is required?
choices: A DBFS mount of the bucket, followed by CREATE TABLE ... USING DELTA with no LOCATION
An external location covering the path, CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE on it, and a LOCATION clause
Only SELECT on the target schema; Unity Catalog finds the path on its own
An instance profile on the cluster, with Unity Catalog turned off for that table
questions.explanation: External tables need a registered external location (backed by a storage credential), CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE on that location, and USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA, and CREATE TABLE on the parents. The LOCATION clause is what makes the table external.

questions.question: Which capabilities are available on Unity Catalog managed tables but not on external tables?
choices: Predictive optimization and automatic liquid clustering
The ability to be queried from SQL warehouses
Row filters and column masks, which can't be applied to external tables
Time travel and ACID transactions, which external Delta tables don't support
questions.explanation: External Delta tables still have ACID transactions, time travel, and fine-grained access control. Managed tables add automatic maintenance (predictive optimization), automatic liquid clustering, metadata caching, and automatic file deletion after the recovery period.

questions.question: An existing external Delta table in Unity Catalog should become a managed table, with minimal downtime and without recreating it. Which command does this?
choices: ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders SET LOCATION MANAGED
CONVERT TO DELTA main.sales.orders MANAGED
ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders SET MANAGED
ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders OWNER TO MANAGED
questions.explanation: SET MANAGED copies the data into managed storage and switches the table over, with only a brief write-blocking phase. It needs Delta format, Databricks Runtime 17.3 LTS or above (or serverless), and ownership or MANAGE. Foreign tables need SET MANAGED MOVE or COPY.

questions.question: A week after running ALTER TABLE ... SET MANAGED, the team finds that an external reader still needs the original path and wants to roll the conversion back. What is possible?
choices: DROP TABLE followed by UNDROP TABLE ... AS EXTERNAL
Nothing; the conversion is permanent the moment it completes
ALTER TABLE ... UNSET MANAGED, within the 14-day window
RESTORE TABLE ... TO EXTERNAL, which works for up to 30 days
questions.explanation: After the conversion, Databricks keeps the old data in the external location for 14 days to allow a rollback with UNSET MANAGED. After that, predictive optimization or a manual VACUUM purges it.

questions.question: A managed table, main.sales.orders, must become an external table at s3://acme-ext/orders/. There is no in-place ALTER for this direction. What is a valid approach?
choices: Move the managed files by hand with dbutils.fs.mv and update the table's path property
Copy it to the external location with CTAS or DEEP CLONE and LOCATION, then drop the original
Run VACUUM on main.sales.orders with a LOCATION pointing at the new path
ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders SET EXTERNAL 's3://acme-ext/orders/'
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog supports converting external to managed (SET MANAGED), and UNSET MANAGED is only a rollback for recently converted tables. To produce an external table from a managed one, copy the data to an external location with CTAS or DEEP CLONE plus LOCATION. Never move the managed files by hand.

questions.question: Where does Unity Catalog store the data files of a managed table?
choices: Always in the workspace's DBFS root, whatever the configuration
In a path the user must give with a LOCATION clause on every CREATE TABLE
In the managed storage location of its schema, catalog, or metastore
On the local disks of whichever cluster created the table
questions.explanation: Managed storage can be configured at the metastore, catalog, or schema level, and the most specific one applies. Because Databricks manages the paths, you don't give a LOCATION for managed tables.

questions.question: Which file formats can Unity Catalog external tables use?
choices: Only Parquet and Delta Lake
Only Delta Lake
DELTA, CSV, JSON, AVRO, PARQUET, ORC, and TEXT
Any format, including Excel workbooks and PDFs
questions.explanation: External tables can register several file formats. Managed tables are Delta Lake (or Apache Iceberg), which is the recommended default for performance and maintenance.

questions.question: A user dropped the managed table main.hr.employees by mistake two days ago, and the default retention settings are unchanged. How can it be recovered?
choices: CREATE TABLE main.hr.employees FROM TRASH
UNDROP TABLE main.hr.employees
It can't be recovered; dropped managed tables are deleted immediately
RESTORE TABLE main.hr.employees TO VERSION AS OF 0
questions.explanation: Dropped managed tables stay recoverable for the retention window (7 days by default), and UNDROP TABLE brings them back with their data and metadata. RESTORE works only on tables that still exist.

questions.question: How can an engineer check whether main.sales.orders is a managed or an external table, and where its files are?
choices: Run DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED and check the Type and Location fields
Run SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE main.sales.orders
Run DESCRIBE HISTORY main.sales.orders and read the first version
Run SELECT COUNT(*) FROM main.sales.orders and compare it with the file count
questions.explanation: DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED, or Catalog Explorer's details tab, shows the table type, the storage location, the provider, the owner, and other metadata.

questions.question: When does Databricks recommend an external table over a managed table?
choices: When data must stay in place for other tools to read directly
Whenever the data has to support time travel queries
Whenever the table needs row filters or column masks applied
Whenever the table grows larger than 1 TB of data
questions.explanation: Databricks recommends managed tables in most cases (automatic optimization, lower cost, faster queries). External tables suit registering existing data in place, or data that other systems must access directly by path.

questions.question: What is the minimum set of privileges the analysts group needs to query the table main.sales.orders?
choices: MODIFY on main.sales.orders and USE SCHEMA on main.sales
ALL PRIVILEGES on the main catalog
SELECT on main.sales.orders, and nothing else
USE CATALOG on main, USE SCHEMA on main.sales, and SELECT on the table
questions.explanation: To read a table you need SELECT on it plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on its parents. Without the USE privileges, a SELECT grant on the table alone isn't enough.

questions.question: Which SQL statement gives the analysts account group read access to main.sales.orders?
choices: ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders ADD READER `analysts`
GRANT `analysts` SELECT ON main.sales.orders
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE main.sales.orders TO `analysts`
GRANT READ ON TABLE main.sales.orders FOR `analysts`
questions.explanation: The syntax is GRANT <privilege> ON <securable type> <name> TO <principal>, with principal names in backticks. Granting to groups rather than individuals is the recommended practice.

questions.question: The contractors group should no longer be able to modify main.sales.orders. Which statement removes that privilege?
choices: REVOKE MODIFY ON TABLE main.sales.orders FROM `contractors`
DENY MODIFY ON TABLE main.sales.orders TO `contractors`, which Unity Catalog enforces
GRANT NO MODIFY ON TABLE main.sales.orders TO `contractors`
REVOKE MODIFY ON TABLE main.sales.orders TO `contractors`
questions.explanation: REVOKE ... FROM removes a privilege that was granted. In Unity Catalog, privileges that aren't granted are denied by default, and the DENY statement applies only to the legacy hive_metastore catalog.

questions.question: An admin runs GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA main.sales TO `analysts`. Which tables can the analysts read, provided they also have USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA?
choices: Only the tables that existed when the grant was made
No tables; SELECT can only be granted on individual tables
Every table in every schema of the main catalog
Every current and future table and view in main.sales
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog privileges flow down the hierarchy: a grant on a catalog or schema applies to all current and future child objects. That is why grants at higher levels are powerful, and why they should be made deliberately.

questions.question: A security lead asks for a DENY SELECT statement on a Unity Catalog table to block a group. What is the correct response?
choices: Use DENY on the schema, which Unity Catalog supports, but not on tables
Run DENY ALL PRIVILEGES ON METASTORE, which blocks the group everywhere
DENY works only in hive_metastore; in Unity Catalog, revoke the grants instead
Run DENY SELECT ON TABLE ...; Unity Catalog always lets DENY override grants
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog grants are additive, with no explicit DENY statement. Access is removed with REVOKE wherever it was granted, including at parent levels and through group memberships. Unity Catalog's ABAC DENY policies (Beta) can deny only MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL.

questions.question: In the legacy hive_metastore catalog with table access control, a user has been DENIED SELECT on a table and is also GRANTED SELECT through a group. How is this resolved, and how is the DENY undone?
choices: The most recent statement wins, whether it is a DENY or a GRANT
DENY wins over any grant, and is undone with REVOKE
The GRANT wins, because grants through groups always take precedence
DENY is undone with GRANT ... WITH OVERRIDE
questions.explanation: For hive_metastore objects, a DENY overrides any explicit or implicit grant, and denying on a parent also denies on its children. REVOKE removes the DENY. This behavior is legacy and doesn't carry over to Unity Catalog securables.

questions.question: A production job runs as a service principal that needs to write to main.silver.orders. How is the service principal named in a GRANT statement?
choices: By the email address of the user who created it
By prefixing its display name with sp:, for example TO sp:etl-bot
By its application ID, in backticks
Service principals can't receive Unity Catalog grants; add them to the admins group
questions.explanation: Users are named by email, groups by group name, and service principals by application ID, for example GRANT MODIFY ON TABLE main.silver.orders TO `6f1b2c3d-...`. Service principals are the recommended identities for production jobs and CI/CD.

questions.question: How can a table owner give the analysts group read access to a table without writing SQL?
choices: Edit the table's properties to add analysts=read
Add the analysts group to the cluster's Can Attach To permission
Open the table's notebook and share the notebook with the analysts group
In Catalog Explorer, use the table's Permissions tab to grant SELECT
questions.explanation: Catalog Explorer has a Permissions tab on each securable for granting and revoking privileges, which is the UI equivalent of GRANT and REVOKE. The group also needs USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on the parents.

questions.question: Which Unity Catalog privilege allows inserting, updating, and deleting rows in a table?
choices: WRITE TABLE
MODIFY
EXECUTE
SELECT
questions.explanation: MODIFY is the composite privilege for adding, updating, and deleting data. Finer-grained INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE privileges exist in Beta. WRITE VOLUME applies to volumes, and EXECUTE applies to functions and models.

questions.question: A team lead is granted ALL PRIVILEGES on the schema main.marketing. Which ability does that grant NOT include?
choices: MODIFY on the tables in the schema
The MANAGE privilege
SELECT on the tables in the schema
CREATE TABLE in the schema
questions.explanation: ALL PRIVILEGES covers the applicable privileges, but deliberately excludes MANAGE (as well as READ METADATA and the external access privileges). MANAGE allows granting and revoking privileges and transferring ownership, so managing access needs MANAGE or ownership.

questions.question: The engineer who owns main.sales.orders is leaving the company. Ownership should go to the data_engineers group. Which statement does this?
choices: ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders SET TBLPROPERTIES ('owner' = 'data_engineers')
REVOKE OWNER ON TABLE main.sales.orders FROM CURRENT_USER
GRANT OWNERSHIP ON TABLE main.sales.orders TO `data_engineers`
ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders OWNER TO `data_engineers`
questions.explanation: Ownership is transferred with ALTER <securable> ... OWNER TO <principal>. Owners have full control over their objects, and making a group the owner avoids orphaned objects when people leave.

questions.question: An auditor wants to see which principals hold which privileges on main.sales.orders. Which command shows this?
choices: DESCRIBE HISTORY main.sales.orders
SHOW TBLPROPERTIES main.sales.orders
LIST PERMISSIONS main.sales.orders
SHOW GRANTS ON TABLE main.sales.orders
questions.explanation: SHOW GRANTS lists the privileges granted on a securable, and can be filtered to one principal (SHOW GRANTS `user` ON ...). It doesn't show the effects of ABAC policies; SHOW EFFECTIVE POLICIES covers those.

questions.question: Analysts should be able to discover which tables exist in a catalog, and see their metadata in Catalog Explorer, without being able to read any data. Which privilege fits?
choices: USE CATALOG together with MODIFY
SELECT
READ VOLUME
BROWSE
questions.explanation: BROWSE lets principals discover objects and view their metadata, without needing USE CATALOG or USE SCHEMA, and without data access. Users can then request access to what they find.

questions.question: The function region_filter(region STRING) RETURNS BOOLEAN already exists. How is it attached as a row filter on the region column of main.sales.orders?
choices: GRANT FILTER region_filter ON TABLE main.sales.orders TO `analysts`
ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders SET ROW FILTER region_filter ON (region)
ALTER TABLE main.sales.orders ALTER COLUMN region SET MASK region_filter
CREATE ROW POLICY region_filter ON main.sales.orders USING region
questions.explanation: A row filter is a SQL UDF that returns BOOLEAN and is evaluated for every row at query time; rows where it returns FALSE are hidden. It is attached with SET ROW FILTER ... ON (columns) and removed with ALTER TABLE ... DROP ROW FILTER.

questions.question: The mask function ssn_mask(ssn STRING) RETURNS STRING exists. Which statement applies it to the ssn column of main.hr.employees?
choices: UPDATE main.hr.employees SET ssn = ssn_mask(ssn)
ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees SET ROW FILTER ssn_mask ON (ssn)
ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees ALTER COLUMN ssn SET MASK ssn_mask
ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees MASK COLUMN ssn WITH ssn_mask
questions.explanation: A column mask is a UDF that takes the column value and returns the value or a masked version of it. It is applied at query time, so the stored data doesn't change. It is removed with ALTER COLUMN ssn DROP MASK.

questions.question: Members of the hr_admins group should see full SSNs, and everyone else only the last four digits. Which mask function body does this?
choices: RETURN CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('hr_admins') THEN ssn ELSE concat('***-**-', right(ssn, 4)) END
RETURN is_account_group_member('hr_admins') AND right(ssn, 4) IS NOT NULL
RETURN IF(is_member('everyone'), ssn, concat('***-**-', right(ssn, 4)))
RETURN CASE WHEN current_user() = 'hr_admins' THEN ssn ELSE concat('***-**-', right(ssn, 4)) END
questions.explanation: Mask functions usually branch on group membership. is_account_group_member checks account-level groups, which is what Unity Catalog uses. current_user() returns a user's identity, never a group's, and a function that returns BOOLEAN is a row filter, not a mask.

questions.question: Why should row filter and column mask functions in Unity Catalog generally use is_account_group_member() rather than is_member()?
choices: is_member() works only inside Python UDFs, not SQL UDFs
is_account_group_member() is faster because it caches the result for a whole day
is_member() always returns TRUE for workspace admins, and is_account_group_member() never does
It checks account-level groups; is_member() checks workspace-local groups
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog works with account-level identities, so logic based on is_account_group_member stays consistent across every workspace attached to the metastore. is_member refers to legacy workspace-level groups.

questions.question: Members of us_sales should see only rows where region = 'US', and members of admins should see every row. Which row filter function body does this?
choices: RETURN region = 'US' OR is_account_group_member('us_sales')
RETURN is_account_group_member('admins') AND (is_account_group_member('us_sales') OR region = 'US')
RETURN CASE WHEN is_account_group_member('us_sales') THEN 'US' ELSE region END
RETURN is_account_group_member('admins') OR (is_account_group_member('us_sales') AND region = 'US')
questions.explanation: A row filter returns TRUE for the rows that should be visible. Admins get TRUE for every row, us_sales members only for US rows, and everyone else sees nothing. A filter must return BOOLEAN, so returning a region value doesn't work.

questions.question: Which statement about tables with row filters or column masks is correct?
choices: They can be read through the Iceberg REST catalog without any restrictions
Masks permanently rewrite the stored data the first time it is read
They can't be queried from SQL warehouses, only from notebooks
They don't support time travel or clones, and only owners or MANAGE holders change them
questions.explanation: Documented limitations include no time travel, no clones, and no access through the Iceberg REST catalog or Unity REST APIs. Filters and masks are evaluated at query time, and managing them requires ownership or MANAGE on the table.

questions.question: Row filter functions on large tables are slowing queries down. Which guidance does Databricks give for writing these functions?
choices: Keep them simple, deterministic SQL UDFs that never throw errors
Call an external REST API in each function to look up permissions
Use non-deterministic functions so that each query gets a fresh result
Write them in Python, because Python UDFs are optimized best
questions.explanation: Filters and masks run for every row at query time. Simple SQL expressions are optimizable, while Python UDFs and complex logic are slower and give the optimizer fewer opportunities.

questions.question: A team wants to share a curated subset of a table's columns, with an email column redacted for non-members of a group, without attaching a filter or mask to the base table. Which approach fits?
choices: A materialized view with a SCHEDULE clause and no grants
A dynamic view that uses is_account_group_member() in a CASE expression
A temporary view that each user creates in their own session
An external table over a copy of the data with the column deleted
questions.explanation: Dynamic views put access logic in the view definition and suit curated or transformed data sharing. Table-level filters and masks protect the base table itself, and ABAC policies centralize the rules across many tables.

questions.question: Masking must be removed from the ssn column of main.hr.employees. Which statement does this?
choices: ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees ALTER COLUMN ssn DROP MASK
ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees UNSET TBLPROPERTIES ('mask')
ALTER TABLE main.hr.employees DROP ROW FILTER
DROP FUNCTION ssn_mask CASCADE TO TABLE
questions.explanation: Masks are added and removed per column with SET MASK and DROP MASK. Row filters are removed at the table level with ALTER TABLE ... DROP ROW FILTER.

questions.question: How are row filters and column masks applied when a user queries a protected table?
choices: Only to users outside the account's admins group, which can't be changed
Only in notebooks; SQL warehouses ignore them
At query time, based on who runs the query; stored data is unchanged
Once, when the filter is created, by rewriting the table's data files
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog evaluates the filter and mask UDFs during query execution, using functions such as current_user() and is_account_group_member(). Different users querying the same table can therefore see different rows and values.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of Unity Catalog attribute-based access control (ABAC) policies over per-table row filters and column masks?
choices: ABAC policies encrypt the data files at rest with a per-user key
ABAC policies make queries run faster by caching filtered results
One tag-based policy covers every matching table, including ones tagged later
ABAC policies remove the need for USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA grants
questions.explanation: A policy might, for example, mask every column tagged pii in every table of a schema tagged HR. Newly tagged objects are covered without extra work, whereas a per-table filter has to be attached to each table separately.

questions.question: What are governed tags in Databricks?
choices: Account-level tags with controlled values and assignment, used by ABAC
Free-form key-value labels that any user can add to any table
Workspace-local tags that apply only to clusters and jobs
Tags that Databricks generates automatically from column statistics
questions.explanation: Governed tags enforce consistency: the allowed values are controlled, and who can create, edit, and assign the tags is permission-managed. They show a lock icon in the UI. Ungoverned tags can still be created alongside them.

questions.question: Which policy masks every column tagged pii=ssn, for all tables in the schema prod.customers, for us_analysts but not for admins?
choices: ALTER SCHEMA prod.customers SET MASK ssn_to_last4 ON COLUMNS TAGGED has_tag_value('pii', 'ssn') TO us_analysts EXCEPT admins
GRANT MASK ssn_to_last4 ON SCHEMA prod.customers TO us_analysts EXCEPT admins WHEN has_tag_value('pii', 'ssn')
CREATE POLICY mask_ssn ON SCHEMA prod.customers ROW FILTER ssn_to_last4 TO us_analysts EXCEPT admins FOR TABLES WHEN has_tag_value('pii', 'ssn') USING COLUMNS (ssn)
CREATE POLICY mask_ssn ON SCHEMA prod.customers COLUMN MASK ssn_to_last4 TO us_analysts EXCEPT admins FOR TABLES MATCH COLUMNS has_tag_value('pii', 'ssn') AS ssn ON COLUMN ssn
questions.explanation: A column mask policy names the mask UDF, the principals (TO, with optional EXCEPT), FOR TABLES, an optional WHEN condition on table tags, MATCH COLUMNS with a tag condition and an alias, and ON COLUMN to say which matched column gets masked.

questions.question: In an ABAC row filter policy, what does MATCH COLUMNS has_tag('geo_region') AS region USING COLUMNS (region) do?
choices: It creates a new column called region in every table
It passes the column tagged geo_region in each table to the filter function
It restricts the policy to tables that have a column named geo_region
It grants USE on the geo_region tag to the policy's principals
questions.explanation: MATCH COLUMNS binds columns by their tags rather than their names, so one policy works across tables whose column names differ. USING COLUMNS passes the matched columns to the UDF. A policy can have up to 3 MATCH COLUMNS expressions.

questions.question: At which levels can ABAC row filter and column mask policies be attached, and how do they reach child objects?
choices: A catalog, schema, or table; child objects inherit the policy
Only on the workspace, and it applies to every metastore
Only on tables, so every table needs its own separate policy
Only on individual columns, with no inheritance at all
questions.explanation: Policies attach to securables, and those on parent scopes automatically apply to descendants. SHOW EFFECTIVE POLICIES lists the policies, inherited ones included, that apply to an object.

questions.question: What does a user need in order to create an ABAC policy on the catalog prod?
choices: Workspace admin rights; no Unity Catalog privileges are needed
MANAGE (or ownership) on prod, plus EXECUTE on the policy's UDF
Only SELECT on every table in the prod catalog
CREATE EXTERNAL LOCATION on the metastore
questions.explanation: Creating, editing, and deleting policies requires MANAGE or ownership on the securable the policy attaches to. The filtering or masking logic lives in a Unity Catalog UDF the user can EXECUTE, or in an inline SQL function. Policies also need Databricks Runtime 16.4 or above, or serverless compute.

questions.question: In an ABAC policy written as TO `account users` EXCEPT `compliance_team`, what do members of compliance_team see?
choices: The original data, because EXCEPT exempts them from the policy
Nothing, because EXCEPT blocks them from the table completely
Only the rows that the policy's WHEN clause matches
Masked data, plus an audit warning about each query
questions.explanation: TO names the principals the policy applies to, and EXCEPT exempts specific principals, such as admins or compliance staff, who then see the original data.

questions.question: An ABAC row filter policy on a schema has no WHEN clause. Which tables does it apply to?
choices: Every table in the schema, because WHEN defaults to TRUE
Only tables created after the policy was defined
Only the tables that carry at least one governed tag
No tables, until a WHEN condition is added
questions.explanation: WHEN filters which tables in the scope the policy applies to, usually by their tags (has_tag, has_tag_value). If it is omitted, the policy applies to every table in its scope.

questions.question: Governance wants to stop table owners in the finance catalog (other than data_admins) from granting access to tables tagged sensitive, even though owners can normally grant privileges. Which Unity Catalog feature does this?
choices: DENY SELECT ON CATALOG finance TO `account users` EXCEPT `data_admins`
An ABAC DENY policy denying MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL on tables tagged sensitive
REVOKE OWNERSHIP ON CATALOG finance FROM `account users`
A column mask on every sensitive column that returns NULL to non-admins
questions.explanation: ABAC DENY policies attach at the metastore, catalog, or schema level and override any grant of the denied privilege, ownership included. Currently MANAGE ACCESS CONTROL is the only privilege they can deny; SELECT and MODIFY can't be denied this way.

questions.question: SHOW GRANTS on a table shows that a user holds SELECT, yet the user sees masked values. Which command reveals the policies affecting that table, inherited ones included?
choices: DESCRIBE HISTORY
SHOW TBLPROPERTIES
SHOW EFFECTIVE POLICIES
SHOW FUNCTIONS
questions.explanation: SHOW GRANTS lists privilege grants but doesn't reflect ABAC policies. SHOW EFFECTIVE POLICIES shows the row filter, column mask, and DENY policies that apply to an object, including those inherited from its catalog or schema.
